chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Wuhaib ibn Hafs, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام.
I asked him about a غلام who entered the house of some people playing, then fell into their well. Are they liable?
He said: «They are not liable; but if they are suspected, they are liable.»

key_terms.دَارَ: the house or property of a people
key_terms.مُتَّهَمِينَ: under suspicion or accused in a legally relevant sense
key_terms.يَضْمَنُونَ: they bear legal liability or compensation

ai.seo_question: Are people liable if a child falls into their well?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about liability when a child falls into a people's well. The basic ruling is that they are not held liable, unless there is cause for suspicion against them, in which case liability is established.
